question: Suppose \([a\ b]\) denotes the average of \(a\) and \(b,\) and \(\{a\ b\ c\}\) denotes the average of \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c.\) What is the value of the following expression? \[\{\{1 \ 1 \ 0\} \ [0 \ 1] \ 0\}\]
solution:
The inner averages must be evaluated first because their values become entries of the outer average. Using sum divided by number of entries gives
\[
\{1\ 1\ 0\}=\frac{1+1+0}{3}=\frac23,
\qquad [0\ 1]=\frac{0+1}{2}=\frac12.
\]
The outer braces average these two values and \(0\), so there are still three entries. Using a common denominator of \(6\), the expression equals
\[
\frac{\frac23+\frac12+0}{3}
=\frac{7/6}{3}
=\frac7{18}.
\]
The value is \(\frac7{18}\), choice D.
